data.long_meaning: Vedanavi is a unisex name derived from Sanskrit, meaning 'Goddess of Knowledge'. The name Vedanavi carries the meaning “Knowledge Goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vedanavi usually hope their child will grow to embody knowledge goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Vedanavi is mentioned in the epic Mahabharata, specifically in the Anushasana Parva or the Book of Instructions, as the name of a young princess who was the wife of the great sage Vyasa.
historical_references.context: Vedanavi was an important figure in Hindu mythology and literature, and her name is often mentioned alongside the great sage Vyasa and the epic Mahabharata.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Vedanavi can be found in the Puranas, specifically the Bhagavata Purana. In this text, Vedanavi is mentioned as the name of a princess who was the wife of the sage Markandeya.
historical_references.context: Vedanavi's marriage to Markandeya is described as a significant event in the lineage of sages and is mentioned alongside other important figures in Hindu mythology.
